annotations.text:
A · COMMAND DECK

Dense and data-first. Every habit is one scannable row, and monospaced numerals line up so progress, streak and XP compare straight down the column. Best if you want the whole day readable in a single glance.

Tradeoff: reads like a professional instrument, not a reward. The least game-like of the three.

B · TRAINING LOG

Editorial and calm. Serif display type, generous air, one large percentage per habit. Feels like a premium training journal — the improvement numbers get room to breathe, which suits the weekly review and progress screens.

Tradeoff: fewer habits fit on screen, and the game layer stays quiet.

C · PROGRESSION

Game-system forward but adult. Rank badge, segmented XP track, progress rings, difficulty tiers, and a glow on whichever habit is currently running. The most motivating of the three on a normal day.

Tradeoff: the most visual machinery to maintain, and it can feel busy when the day is full.
